title: Threshold Methods for Anomaly Detection
text: KDE-Weighted method uses kernel density estimation compute density-weighted robust mean. Points high-density regions (normal data) receive higher weights, points low-density regions (potential outliers) receive lower weights.

title: Threshold Methods for Anomaly Detection
text: Density-weighted mean definition: weighted mean using KDE densities: w_i = KDE density point x_i (weight based local density). Intuition: High-density points (normal data cluster) dominate mean, low-density points (outliers) minimal influence. Threshold: : - k = multiplier (default: 3) - σ = standard deviation scores
code: μ_w = Σ(w_i × x_i) / Σw_i 1. Normalize: scores_norm = (scores - min) / (max - min) 2. Compute KDE: kde = KDE(scores_norm) 3. Get density weights: kde_weights = kde(sorted_scores_norm) 4. Weighted vector: vals = kde_weights ⊙ sorted_scores_norm 5. Density-weighted mean: μ_w = sum(vals) / sum(kde_weights) 6. Denormalize: μ_w = μ_w × (max - min) + min 7. Threshold = μ_w + k × σ

title: Threshold Methods for Anomaly Detection
text: Normalize scores [0, 1] Estimate probability density using KDE Interpolate KDE density actual data points (get weights) Compute density-weighted average: Σ(weight × score) / Σweight Denormalize back original scale Use SD scale measure Set threshold = weighted_mean + k × σ

code: - Arithmetic mean: Equal weights for all points - Median: 50% quantile, ignores distribution shape - Density-weighted: Adaptive weights based on local density

title: Threshold Methods for Anomaly Detection
text: MTT (Modified Thompson Tau) statistical test based t-distribution iteratively identifies removes outliers, determines threshold clean normal data.

title: Threshold Methods for Anomaly Detection
text: Thompson Tau statistic: : - n = current sample size - t_α = t-distribution critical value, df = n-2, α/(2n) (Bonferroni correction) - τ = Thompson Tau critical value Decision rule (per iteration): Final threshold: μ_inlier σ_inlier mean SD remaining normal data removing outliers.
code: τ = (t_α × (n-1)) / √(n × (n - 2 + t_α²)) If |x_i - μ| > τ × σ, then x_i is outlier threshold = μ_inlier + 3 × σ_inlier

title: Threshold Methods for Anomaly Detection
code: Initialize: x = all anomaly scores  For each iteration (max max_iter times):   1. Calculate current mean μ and SD σ      2. Find point with maximum deviation:      max_deviation = max(|x_i - μ|)      3. Calculate t-distribution critical value (Bonferroni corrected):      df = n - 2      t_α = qt(1 - α/(2n), df)      4. Calculate Thompson Tau statistic:      τ = (t_α × (n-1)) / √(n × (df + t_α²))      5. Calculate critical threshold:      critical_value = τ × σ      6. Check if maximum deviation point is outlier:      If max_deviation > critical_value:        - Mark as outlier        - Remove from dataset        - Continue to next iteration      Else:        - No more outliers        - Stop iteration  Final threshold calculation:   threshold = mean(remaining normal points) + 3 × sd(remaining normal points)

title: Threshold Methods for Anomaly Detection
text: 1. Statistical rigor Based t-distribution (normal), better small samples: - Small samples: t-distribution heavier tails - Large samples: t-distribution approaches normal - Accounts sample size uncertainty 2. Bonferroni correction avoid multiple comparison problems: ensures overall Type error rate stays α level across multiple tests. 3. Iterative refinement Recalculate mean SD outlier removal: - Avoid outlier contamination parameter estimates - Progressively “clean” dataset - Final threshold based pure normal data 4. Conservative strategy Final 3σ rule: Ensures -detection; truly significant deviations flagged.
code: Significance level: α_adjusted = α / (2n) threshold = μ_inlier + 3 × σ_inlier

title: Threshold Methods for Anomaly Detection
text: Data: [0.50, 0.51, 0.52, 0.53, 0.54, 0.80, 0.85] Iteration 1: Iteration 2: Iteration 3: Final:
code: n = 7, μ = 0.607, σ = 0.145 Maximum deviation point: 0.85, deviation = 0.243  Calculation:   t_0.05/(2×7) = t_0.0036(5) ≈ 3.71   τ = (3.71 × 6) / √(7 × (5 + 3.71²)) ≈ 0.796   critical_value = 0.796 × 0.145 ≈ 0.115  Decision: 0.243 > 0.115 → 0.85 is outlier, remove n = 6, μ = 0.633, σ = 0.152 Maximum deviation point: 0.80, deviation = 0.167  Calculation:   t_0.05/(2×6) = t_0.0042(4) ≈ 3.96   τ ≈ 0.834   critical_value = 0.834 × 0.152 ≈ 0.127  Decision: 0.167 > 0.127 → 0.80 is outlier, remove n = 5, μ = 0.520, σ = 0.016 Maximum deviation point: 0.54, deviation = 0.020  Calculation:   critical_value ≈ 0.015  Decision: 0.020 ≤ 0.015 (marginally, stop) Normal data: [0.50, 0.51, 0.52, 0.53, 0.54] μ_inlier = 0.520 σ_inlier = 0.016 threshold = 0.520 + 3 × 0.016 = 0.568

title: Karcher Mean Thresholding for Anomaly Detection — karcher_threshold
text: Karcher mean (also known Fréchet mean Riemannian center mass) robust geometric method setting thresholds anomaly detection. minimizes sum squared geodesic distances, making particularly effective data non-Euclidean structure, heavy-tailed distributions, extreme outliers.

title: Karcher Mean Thresholding for Anomaly Detection — karcher_threshold
code: set_anomaly_threshold(   object,    method = "karcher",   karcher_multiplier = 3,   karcher_method = "complex",   karcher_max_iter = 100,   karcher_tol = 1e-6 )

title: Karcher Mean Thresholding for Anomaly Detection — karcher_threshold
text: Karcher mean (Frechet mean) \(\mu_K\) defined point minimizes sum squared distances: $$\mu_K = \arg\min_{\mu} \sum_{=1}^{n} d^2(x_i, \mu)$$ \(d(x_i, \mu)\) distance observation \(x_i\) candidate mean \(\mu\). threshold determination, method offers two modes: Complex mode (default): Uses KDE (kernel density estimation)         weighting account data distribution Simple mode: Direct computation weighted arithmetic mean Calculates scale using standard deviation (SD) anomaly scores Sets threshold : \(threshold = \mu_K + m \times SD\) \(m\) multiplier parameter (default: 3).

title: Karcher Mean Thresholding for Anomaly Detection — karcher_threshold
text: Distribution awareness: Complex mode uses KDE weight scores         density, providing better handling non-uniform distributions Geometric optimality: Provides optimal center (Frechet mean)         Euclidean space Flexible computation: Supports simple (fast) complex         (distribution-aware) modes Proven algorithm: Based PyOD KARCH implementation solid         empirical results Theoretical foundation: Grounded Riemannian geometry         Frechet mean theory

title: Karcher Mean Thresholding for Anomaly Detection — karcher_threshold
text: karcher_multiplier Controls threshold strictness. Default: 3 Lower (1-2): sensitive, detects anomalies Higher (3-4): Balanced, standard approach Even higher (>4): conservative, fewer false positives  karcher_method Computation method. Default: "complex" "complex": Uses KDE weighting better distribution fitting "simple": Direct weighted mean computation (faster)  karcher_max_iter Maximum iterations convergence. Default: 100 Increase complex distributions Decrease faster computation simple data  karcher_tol Convergence tolerance. Default: 1e-6 Smaller values: precise slower Larger values: Faster less precise

title: Karcher Mean Thresholding for Anomaly Detection — karcher_threshold
text: implementation follows PyOD KARCH approach: Complex Mode (Default): Normalize anomaly scores [0, 1] Generate kernel density estimation (KDE) using Gaussian kernel Perform element-wise multiplication: KDE values × sorted normalized scores Compute weighted arithmetic mean (Frechet mean Euclidean space) Denormalize back original scale Calculate threshold: Frechet mean + multiplier × SD Simple Mode: Compute weighted arithmetic mean directly scores Calculate threshold: mean + multiplier × SD 1D Euclidean space, Frechet mean simply weighted arithmetic mean.

title: Karcher Mean Thresholding for Anomaly Detection — karcher_threshold
text: Complex mode: \(O(n \log n)\) KDE computation Simple mode: \(O(n)\) direct mean computation Space: \(O(n)\) storing scores KDE values Complex mode slightly slower MAD, provides better distribution fitting
